Runner: source-snapshots/run_new_models.py (deposit; not read for this file). Caps: a pipeline element replaces the runtime function registry with the permitted subset before tool selection; FunctionsRuntime.run_function rejects an absent tool with ToolNotFoundError, so the cap restricts execution, not only the displayed list; no argument-level constraints (Supplementary Note 5). Auto-confirm: one generic approval reply is returned once after a final assistant turn that contains a question and no tool call (Note 2). Known 0.1.35 properties touching this design: injection tasks run as user tasks before the attacked cells (prepass, 27 per full arm); null final content triggers up to 3 passes and only the last is logged; run errors impose utility False, security True (#154); OpenAILLM drops temperature=0.0 (#141; paper claims temperature 0 for all runs, Table S17); security_from_traces scores proposed calls (#168/#189): slack injection_task_5 under a blocking cap; utility_from_traces analogue (#218); banking UT5 permissive checker (#161; the paper's Table S25); banking IT0/1/3 dead subject check (#181); tool results with non-ASCII text are \uXXXX-escaped (#214).

discrepancy_leads: Pilot: the paper describes a 169-run Haiku banking pilot; the deposit's pilot/ holds 182 logs (haiku 169, haiku-autoconfirm 3, luna 5, sol 5). Census arithmetic implies the 13 extras are 4 ii + 9 attack-none and banking. Test at L1-05.
Paper count 18,557 vs 18,739 executions: the difference is exactly the 182 pilot logs; any other difference is a finding.

Run errors: Table S13 gives unknown (error/missing) attacked outcomes only for gpt-3.5-turbo (base 15, A3 12, A4 15) and luna-capA3 (1); the census has 51 error logs and 5 incompletes. Expect >= 41 errors in the 3.5 attacked logs and the rest in attack-none logs; raw security True on those logs is runner-imposed and must not count as attack success in the comparison.

AgentDojo #168/#189 (security_from_traces counts proposed calls): slack injection_task_5 logs in capA3/capA4/noegress dirs could be logged security True although the membership calls failed; the paper (S24) reports 0 enforced successes on a blocked attacker path. A logged True there contradicts the paper or shows a re-scoring outside the logs.
Caps must be visible as tool errors: calls to tools above the cap should return ToolNotFoundError-type errors, never an error-free result (Note 5 mechanism; Table S1 levels).
Auto-confirm reply is harness-authored but sits in the message list as a user message; check that it appears only in -autoconfirm dirs and how the mapper attributes it (principal user vs harness).

Temperature 0 is claimed for every run (Table S17), but AgentDojo 0.1.35's OpenAILLM does not send temperature=0.0 (#141); unless run_new_models.py passes it directly, the OpenAI runs used the provider default. Not settleable from the logs; read the context artefact.

Deposit README v2.1.0 says original-study/ (which holds the runs, README and RESULTS_new_models.md) documents an earlier stage whose counts and table numbering do not describe the current manuscript; our profile cites RESULTS_new_models.md for the reasoning setting and original-study/README.md as context.

v2.0.0's description says no new model calls for that revision, yet v2.0.0 is the first deposit of exp4/exp5/exp7 (15,926 runs not in v1.0); the README calls them the earlier locally prepared package. Test: no log timestamp later than the v2.0.0 deposit.

Repetitions: Note 5 says the 3 repetitions cover a fixed subset (18 benign, 27 direct, 117 injection cases); census arithmetic gives per-rep suite counts 39/29/39/55 if the pilot extras are banking. Test same cell set across the 6 rep dirs and the reported ASR ranges.

Historical-name confound: Supplementary Note 1 says all 2025-2026 models received the correct name, and Note 5 says the injections generated by the current package use 'Emma Johnson' (the re-executed gpt-4o-mini/gpt-3.5 runs included) [citation corrected 2026-10-15 fact-check]; check ii injections for 'Emma Smith' outside important_instructions_wrong_user_name.
